critic_dispositions.basis: The brief concerns an existing offsite copy and asks for copy/restore validation. The final proposal explicitly retrieves the rehearsal package from that existing offsite location; BagIt manifest verification alone does not test that retrieval route.

RFC 8493 describes package layout and integrity manifests, not a write-protection or retention control. The final uses immutable only for the custodian's documented practice. OCFL v1.1 explicitly intends existing version directories not to change when later versions are added.

Issue #51's reporter describes copying from a Mac to an Archivematica transfer server but does not identify that server as Linux. A later comment separately describes an OS X/Linux test. The final separates those observations.
Inventory authority, identifiers, staff usability, path mapping, digest policy, package depth, validator choice and operating cadence require owner decisions or a future bounded pilot.

sources.title: RFC 8493: The BagIt File Packaging Format, version 1.0
sources.observed_operation: Investigator source map records read-only web open/find of the official RFC Editor page. Reviser independently re-opened RFC 8493 and searched the official text for SHA-512, Payload-Oxum and filename normalization at 2026-10-10T04:38:58Z.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: BagIt v1.0 is a filesystem layout for storage and transfer with directly accessible payload files. Each payload manifest must list every payload file exactly once. Complete and valid have format-specific definitions; valid means complete and all listed manifest checksums verify. Tools must support SHA-256 and SHA-512; SHA-512 creation default is a SHOULD. Payload-Oxum is a quick incomplete-bag check, not a replacement for checksum validation. The RFC discusses path interoperability differences and says BagIt is not designed against active attacks. It does not specify custodian write-protection or retention enforcement.
sources.applicability: Suitable readable packaging and byte/path checking for this small pilot. It does not decide gallery asset identity, registrar completeness, custody or restore success.

reviser_recheck.observed_operation: Read-only web open/find on the official RFC Editor page.
reviser_recheck.rechecked_claims: Direct payload access and layout, complete/valid distinction, payload manifest requirements, SHA-256/SHA-512 MUST support and SHA-512 SHOULD default, Payload-Oxum scope, active-attack limit, and filesystem/path interoperability cautions.

sources.observed_operation: Investigator source map records read-only web open/find of the official version-pinned specification. Reviser independently re-opened the official spec and searched for immutable/version directory passages at 2026-10-10T04:38:58Z.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Object identity stays stable across versions; versions are sequential. Root inventory is required; per-version inventories and logs have specified optional/recommended conditions. Existing version directories are intended not to change when later versions are added.
sources.applicability: A credible transparent versioned-object alternative when richer object history or deduplication merits more layout and validation responsibility. It does not determine exhibition completeness or prove a restore.

reviser_recheck.observed_operation: Read-only web open/find on the official pinned specification.
reviser_recheck.rechecked_claims: The specification states that existing version directories are intended to remain unchanged when a later version directory is added.

sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Equal digests calculated with the same algorithm at two points indicate no byte change during that interval. PREMIS describes the check as an Event and its result as eventOutcome and says this procedure alone does not address object integrity or authenticity.
sources.applicability: Supports event-log concepts and the separation of digest evidence from authorship, custody and authenticity. The proposal is not PREMIS conformance.
